$comment: Swappable voice models. A model is DATA here, not code — add one by adding an entry. `kind`: tts (speak) | stt (listen) | duplex (full-duplex speak+listen at once). `active*` picks the current provider per capability; 'auto' = best available that passes its health check; 'none' = off. Override per-machine at ~/.agent-workspace/voice-providers.json.

providers.label: Browser speech synthesis
providers.notes: Zero install — the page speaks via the Web Speech API. Works on a fresh clone; the fallback when nothing local is set up.

providers.label: Piper (local neural TTS)
providers.install: pip install --user piper-tts && download a voice .onnx (e.g. en_US-amy-medium) then set PIPER_MODEL to its path
providers.notes: Small, fast, fully offline. Good default local voice on modest hardware.

providers.label: Kokoro (local neural, natural — warm HTTP server)
providers.install: pip install --user kokoro-onnx soundfile flask; model+voices in ~/.local/share/kokoro; run ~/.local/bin/kokoro-server.py (started by start-voice-stack.sh).
providers.notes: Natural neural voice; ~2s synth on CPU (faster on GPU). Streamed to the browser like piper. The nicer-sounding local default.

providers.label: Chatterbox (Resemble, real-time + cloning)
providers.install: pip install --user chatterbox-tts; needs a GPU for real-time.
providers.notes: Real-time generative audio with voice cloning, permissive license. Uses the same generic CLI adapter as kokoro.

providers.label: espeak-ng (robotic, always-there fallback)
providers.notes: Last-resort offline voice; robotic but never fails.

providers.label: whisper.cpp (local, GPU-accelerated)
providers.notes: The existing STT path. Accurate, fully offline.

providers.label: faster-whisper (CTranslate2)
providers.install: pip install --user faster-whisper; runs on GPU or CPU.
providers.notes: Faster Whisper reimplementation. Drop-in for the whisper engine.

providers.label: NVIDIA Parakeet TDT (streaming, ultra-low latency)
providers.install: NVIDIA NeMo + parakeet-tdt checkpoint; best on the 5090. RNN-T, RTFx > 2000, true streaming.
providers.notes: The pick for the streaming pipeline lane. Lights up when NeMo + the checkpoint are present.

providers.label: Moonshine (edge/CPU)
providers.notes: Smallest footprint; good for the laptop or CPU-only.

providers.label: Codex app-server realtime (remote)
providers.notes: The full-duplex path that ships today — browser STT -> appendText -> Codex thread -> spoken back. Reasoning + tools, remote.

providers.label: NVIDIA PersonaPlex (full-duplex, LOCAL)
providers.install: git clone github.com/NVIDIA/personaplex; ~19GB BF16 (fits the 5090), 8-16GB quantized via moshi.cpp (fits the 16GB laptop). Serves a web UI at localhost:8998.
providers.notes: Best OPEN local full-duplex: ~70ms speaker-switch. Voice-only (no tools). Lights up when the server is reachable.

providers.label: X-Talk (open full-duplex framework)
providers.install: Pure-Python cascaded full-duplex framework (STT+LLM+TTS with barge-in). Lighter than PersonaPlex.
providers.notes: Newer (mid-2026) open framework; swap the endpoint and it works through the same adapter.
